plan.title: Exact 0.119.5 bootstrap can resolve core 0.119.6 after a compatible release

narratives.Description: The cold-start ladder promises the committed teaching pin but leaves its canonical npm and pnpm commands unversioned, so a learner can select a different CLI release before Module 1. The accepted remedy is deliberately limited to literal-command alignment and verifier coverage; issue #69 retains the separate exact four-package graph remainder.
narratives.Overview:
## Learner context

Independent pre-course tool check on 2026-09-22. Course baseline: `@deftai/directive@0.119.5`, engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.5`.

## Problem

The root cold-start guidance says the version is always the project pin, but its canonical global command is unversioned (`npm i -g @deftai/directive`). The current npm `latest` tag is 0.119.6. Even explicitly requesting the CLI package at 0.119.5 did not reproduce the declared engine baseline:

```text
> npx --yes --package=@deftai/directive@0.119.5 directive --version
@deftai/directive (engine: @deftai/directive-core@0.119.6)
```

`npm view @deftai/directive@0.119.5 dependencies` shows caret ranges for core/content. This is a recurrence of the transitive-resolution mechanism discussed in closed issue #3, now observable at the 0.119.5 teaching baseline.

The Lab 2 fixture avoids the problem by locking the exact CLI/core/content/types graph, and its project-local run correctly reported core 0.119.5. The root bootstrap path does not make that distinction clear.

## Pain experienced

A learner can follow the visible bootstrap guidance before Module 1 and end up on either CLI 0.119.6 or CLI 0.119.5 with core 0.119.6, while every module record claims exact core 0.119.5. That makes baseline failures look like learner mistakes and can make the course's exact-version acceptance impossible outside the locked lab fixture.

## Proposed fix

- Make the root canonical command use the literal project pin.
- Document that the CLI package pin alone is insufficient when its transitive ranges have advanced.
- Provide a reproducible exact-graph bootstrap (lockfile/overrides or a course helper) and a command that asserts CLI, core, content, and types versions before Module 1.
- Add a test that installs from a clean cache after a newer compatible release exists.

## Sanitized environment

- Windows / PowerShell 7.6.5
- Node 26.8.1, npm 11.19.0
- Public npm registry

No Directive source or framework internals were consulted.
narratives.UserStory: As a learner bootstrapping the course repository, I want the canonical npm and pnpm commands to carry the exact teaching pin, so that I do not silently select a different CLI release.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update README cold-start rung 3 so the npm and pnpm global-install commands both carry the literal 0.119.5 package pin without changing Module 1 or adding a root lockfile.
2. Extend scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs to derive the committed package pin and reject either an unpinned or mismatched rung-3 command.
3. Extend scripts/verify-text-portability.test.mjs so the command assertions are exercised with both LF and CRLF content.
4. Run the focused cold-start, teaching-baseline, and portability checks and confirm the change makes no exact-transitive-graph claim reserved for issue #69.

Round 1, fresh critic, seat family claude. Charter: open critique. Reads pinned to `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e`; in envelope: issue body plus comments up to 5785865814.

### Anchor re-verification (measured)

- `README.md:4` says the version to install is always the `package.json` pin. `README.md:8` (rung 3) is the unversioned `npm i -g @deftai/directive`. Confirmed.
- `package.json:40` pins `@deftai/directive` `0.119.5`, with no `overrides` and no lockfile at the root. `references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md:33` says the repo intentionally has no project-local install or lockfile. Confirmed.
- `labs/fixtures/02-disposable-initialization/package.json:9-16` pins the CLI and overrides core, content, and types to `0.119.5`. Confirmed.
- `npm view @deftai/directive@0.119.5 dependencies` gives `directive-core ^0.119.5` and `directive-content ^0.119.5`. Core 0.119.5 gives `directive-types ^0.119.5`. The `latest` dist-tag is now **0.119.7**, not 0.119.6.

/tmp probe: clean caches, isolated npm config, public registry, today.

| Install shape | CLI | core | content | types |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm install --prefix <dir> @deftai/directive@0.119.5` (rung 4 shape) | 0.119.5 | 0.119.7 | 0.119.7 | 0.119.7 |
| `npm install -g --prefix <dir> @deftai/directive@0.119.5` (rung 3 with the literal pin), run from a directory whose `package.json` has the fixture overrides | 0.119.5 | 0.119.7 | 0.119.7 | 0.119.7 |
| `npm install` inside a copy of the Lab 2 fixture manifest | 0.119.5 | 0.119.5 | 0.119.5 | 0.119.5 |

### Findings

**F1. blocks-the-design: a literal pin on the global ladder cannot produce the exact graph.**
Evidence: the probe table. A global install ignores project `overrides`, and a pinned CLI still floats its caret dependencies. Rung 4 (`README.md:9`) already uses `@<pinned>` and still floats. The triage P1 cite does not name it.
Failure mode: proposed-fix bullet 1 ships and every visible command shows `0.119.5`. A learner who follows it still gets core, content, and types at 0.119.7, the same as before, and the pain stays unrelieved.
Disposition: the lean cannot bind on "use the literal pin" as the fix. It must choose where exactness lives. Either (a) exactness is a property of an overrides-bearing project install only, and the host/global CLI is outside the baseline claim, or (b) the course ships a manifest-based bootstrap (a prefix dir with a committed manifest plus overrides) that the pre-Module-1 check runs. A bare `npm i -g …@pin` satisfies neither. Bullet 1 can stay as an alignment fix, but it must not be credited as pain relief.

**F2. sharpens-framing: the exact-graph mechanism already exists. Reuse it; do not invent a second one.**
Evidence: the overrides manifest plus four-package version asserts are already present in `labs/fixtures/02-disposable-initialization/init-lab.mjs:292-298,404`, `05-projection-drift-recovery/projection-lab.mjs:120-121`, `07-scope-lifecycle/lifecycle-lab.mjs:69-70,277`, `10-implementation-golden-path/implementation-lab.mjs:98-99,314`, and `11-testing-gates-and-evidence/gates-lab.mjs:112-113`. `scripts/teaching-baseline.mjs` couples the README marker to the root pin. `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` (`npm run check:cold-start-readme`) already asserts the cold-start block and calls `assertTeachingBaselinePin`.
Failure mode: a new "course helper" plus a new assert command creates a sixth copy of the graph check, and the copies drift on the next baseline bump.
Disposition: scope the pre-Module-1 check as a reuse of the fixture manifest and its asserts (or a shared extraction). Scope any README-text change as an extension of `check:cold-start-readme`, for example "rung 3 and rung 4 carry the literal pin". Neither needs a new gate.

**F3. sharpens-framing: the proposed regression test can pass vacuously.**
Evidence: bullet 4 depends on registry state ("after a newer compatible release exists"). That is true today (0.119.7) only by accident. The authoring host's global install reports exact 0.119.5 for all four packages because it was installed before 0.119.6 shipped. The measured host therefore masks the defect through stale state.
Failure mode: after the next baseline bump to `latest`, no newer release exists. A floating install and an exact install then resolve the same graph, and the test goes green without exercising the hole. A test on a warm-cache authoring host passes for the same reason.
Disposition: state the test as two parts. First, assert the precondition: `npm view` shows a release newer than the pin in the same caret range, or the test reports "not exercised" and does not pass. Then assert that the course's bootstrap path yields the exact four-package graph from a clean cache. Do not frame the test around 0.119.6.

**F4. sharpens-framing: the cold-start block is the sanctioned upstream #2273 v1 text. Record local divergence or an upstream report as a choice.**
Evidence: `README.md:1` and `README.md:14` carry `deft:cold-start-bootstrap v1 (#2273)` markers. Completed scope issue 2 added the block as "the sanctioned … global-first ladder". The 0.119.5 engine's own ladder already prints the pinned form: `npm i -g @deftai/directive@${pin}` (`directive-core/dist/resolution/engine-ladder.js:76`). I found no writer that rewrites the README block in the 0.119.5 engine, so a local edit is not known to be overwritten.
Failure mode: a local edit fixes rung 3 here, while upstream text and caret ranges stay the root cause. The next sanctioned-block refresh or baseline bump reintroduces the drift, and closed issue 3's recurrence repeats.
Disposition: the lean should say what it changes locally (training-owned text plus the check) and what it reports upstream (caret ranges on an exact-version teaching dependency, and the unversioned rung 3). It must not claim the local edit fixes the transitive mechanism.

**F5. footnote:** `@deftai/directive-types` is not a direct CLI dependency. It arrives through core's `^0.119.5`. The probe shows content and types float with core, not only core. The issue's pain text mentions core only.

**F6. footnote:** the issue title and bullet 4 name 0.119.6. The measured `latest` is 0.119.7. Titles tied to a version go stale. The mechanism is "any newer compatible release".

### Road not taken and steelman

The strongest rejected position: declare the host/global CLI outside the baseline claim (option F1a) and change only the prose. Labs already prove the project-local binary (`curriculum/modules/02-installation-and-anatomy.md:357`), and Module 2 already refuses `@latest` as out of boundary. This is the cheapest and most consistent option.

I rejected it as the whole fix because every module header cites "engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.5`" with no scope qualifier. The pre-course tool check in the issue is exactly where a learner reads that claim against a global CLI.

What would flip my verdict: if the lean scopes each module header to "project-local fixture engine" and the pre-course check runs the fixture's binary instead of the global one, then option F1a relieves the pain on its own, and F2's reuse is the whole implementation.

The injection / swarm lens does not fire. The target changes install guidance and a test, not authority, prompts, identity, concurrency, worktrees, or shared state.

audit-targets: none

Round 1, fresh open critique. I read issue 63's body and only comments through 5785865814. I rechecked the Stop 1 anchors with `git show a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e:<path>`: `README.md:4-9`, `package.json:40`, and `labs/fixtures/02-disposable-initialization/package.json:9-16`. I copied the root and Lab 2 manifests into separate `/tmp` directories and ran `npm install` with separate empty npm configs, fresh per-install caches, and `--ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`. The root resolved CLI 0.119.5 with core/content/types 0.119.7; Lab 2 resolved all four at 0.119.5.

### 1. A pinned global command does not make the bootstrap exact (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence: `README.md:4-9` stops at a working `directive doctor` on rung 1, accepts an engine *at or above* the pin on rung 2, uses the unpinned global command on rung 3, and pins only the CLI package on rung 4. The published 0.119.5 CLI/core dependency ranges are `^0.119.5` (`npm view`); the clean-cache root probe above resolved the newer transitive graph. The root package has no lockfile (`references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md:31-34`). npm applies `overrides` only in the install root, so adding them solely to this repository's package does not govern `npm i -g` or `npx` ([npm package.json docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json/#overrides)).

Failure mode: changing rung 3 to `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.119.5` leaves three other accepted paths and transitive resolution able to report “bootstrapped” with a nonbaseline graph. `doctor` success and a CLI pin are not exact-graph evidence.

Disposition: decide whether this ladder is an operational agent bootstrap or the learner's exact teaching path. If it promises the latter, every accepted rung needs an installed four-package assertion and a reproducible install root with overrides or an equivalent lock. Keep the version check attached to the executable selected, not only to `package.json`.

### 2. A required pre-Module 1 install crosses the learner boundary (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence: Module 1's starting check explicitly requires no installation or command recovery (`curriculum/modules/01-what-directive-is.md:28-40`). The course map forbids installing lab tooling in this checkout (`curriculum/README.md:35-37`), and Module 2 calls a host-global `npm i -g` outside its disposable boundary (`curriculum/modules/02-installation-and-anatomy.md:210-222`). The README cold-start block is also agent-followed authority, while a global npm install changes shared host state.

Failure mode: a mandatory four-package assertion before Module 1 makes a learner with no CLI install one before the course teaches or guards the disposable path; an agent could treat the root bootstrap as that learner exercise and mutate the host or authored checkout.

Disposition: identify the audience for the root cold-start guidance. Preserve Module 1 as conceptual. Put the learner's exact install and assertion in the guarded Lab 2 path, or make a pre-course probe explicitly optional and read-only. Give an authoring agent's operational bootstrap its own clearly stated success condition.

### 3. The regression gap is the root path, not Lab 2 (`sharpens-framing`)

Evidence: `init-lab.mjs:288-304,384-404` already verifies all four *installed* packages after a fresh local install, and `scripts/init-lab.test.mjs:173-198` exercises it. Its focused install test passed in this pass with 0.119.7 available. By contrast, `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` checks the README block's structure, and `scripts/teaching-baseline.mjs` compares the README declaration to the top-level package pin; both checks passed while the root clean-cache probe resolved 0.119.7 transitives.

Failure mode: adding another Lab 2 install test can stay green while the cold-start command still produces the wrong graph.

Disposition: exercise the proposed root/bootstrap route as the regression subject, with a clean cache and four installed-version checks. Reuse Lab 2's installed-graph guard rather than designing a second version rule; include a newer-compatible dependency case so a CLI-only pin fails visibly.

Road not taken: pinning only the global CLI command is a small, appealing edit. It would become sufficient if the published CLI itself fixed its transitive graph and every accepted bootstrap route verified that graph. The current caret ranges and fresh install falsify those conditions.

audit-targets: none

Round-1 fresh open critique of issue 63. In-envelope: issue body, Stop 1 comment 5785827790, panel-deposit 5785865814. Dispatch SHA `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e` (dest HEAD detached there). Tree reads from that SHA. Live npm and two isolated `/tmp` installs re-checked the version claims.

## 1. Canonical global install cannot carry the existing exact-graph lock
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence. `npm view @deftai/directive@0.119.5 dependencies` returns `"@deftai/directive-core": "^0.119.5"` and `"@deftai/directive-content": "^0.119.5"`. An isolated `npm install` of root-shaped `"@deftai/directive": "0.119.5"` with no `overrides` resolved CLI 0.119.5 and core/content/types 0.119.7; `./node_modules/.bin/directive --version` printed `engine: @deftai/directive-core@0.119.7`. The same manifest plus the Lab 2 `overrides` block resolved all four packages to 0.119.5 and printed engine 0.119.5. Those `overrides` live on a project `package.json`. README.md:8 canonical command is `npm i -g @deftai/directive` into the host-global prefix. A registry-package global install does not apply this repository's `overrides`. All six `labs/fixtures/*/package.json` files already carry that field. `labs/fixtures/02-disposable-initialization/init-lab.mjs` `verifyManifestPin` / `verifyInstalledGraph` fail closed unless the four installed versions match. `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` and `scripts/teaching-baseline.test.mjs` both passed on this SHA with the unversioned command still in place and root `package.json` still CLI-pin-only (`assertTeachingBaselinePin` couples the README teaching-baseline marker to `devDependencies["@deftai/directive"]` only).

Failure mode. Binding proposed-fix bullet 1 (put the CLI pin on the canonical command) leaves caret resolution in place. Those two gates stay green after a CLI-only README edit. The engine-baseline half of Stop 1 P1 remains: a learner or agent who follows the visible bootstrap still runs core 0.119.7 while every module record claims exact core 0.119.5.

Disposition. Bind hole B (exact graph) to a project-local manifest that uses the existing fixture `overrides` pattern. Bind hole A (unversioned latest CLI) as a separate README/agent-recovery edit. Keep the #2273 global-first ladder as payload-independent recovery of a running binary.

## 2. Cold-start rungs 1–2 accept an above-pin engine before rung 3 runs
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. README.md:6 rung 1: if `directive doctor` runs, skip the rest. README.md:7 rung 2: use `.deft/.cli/<platform>` when it is "at or above" the `package.json` pin. Live `npm view @deftai/directive version` is 0.119.7 (core/content/types match). A host that already has 0.119.6 or 0.119.7 never reaches a rewritten rung 3. Module 1 is command-free. `curriculum/README.md` prerequisites name Node/Git/gh/npm/Task/uv and do not require a global Directive install before Module 1. Lab 2 already asserts the four-package graph on the disposable path.

Failure mode. A Bound-remedy that only edits the canonical command still lets the first working newer binary satisfy cold-start, while module records keep claiming exact core 0.119.5.

Disposition. Treat #2273 as "get a running `directive`". Put the four-package assert on a project-local path that still runs when a newer binary is already on PATH. If pre-Module-1 proof is in scope, name that assert as its own surface.

## 3. New helper, root lockfile, and a "newer release exists" test fight current machinery
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. `references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md:33` records a pin and says the training repository intentionally contains no project-local install or lockfile. Root `package.json` has the CLI pin and no `overrides`. Fixture helpers already install from the public registry in disposable directories and assert CLI/core/content/types. `.github/workflows/content-contract.yml` runs content verifiers with no `@deftai/directive` install. `scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs` rejects host-global `npm i -g @deftai/directive` inside learner-executable fences. Module 2 and Lab 2 quote `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` as out-of-boundary doctor advice.

Failure mode. Binding "lockfile/overrides or a course helper" as an OR lets an implementer add a root lockfile (silent recut of SOURCE-BASELINE) or a seventh helper that duplicates `verify-pin` / `verifyInstalledGraph`. A test that is green only while a newer compatible release exists goes silent the next time `latest` equals the pin.

Disposition. If the training repo must lock a graph, add the existing `overrides` field to the root pin and recut the SOURCE-BASELINE sentence as a deliberate policy change. Reuse the fixture install assertions for mixed-graph coverage. Leave `content-contract.yml` as a content lane unless that workflow is explicitly expanded to install.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes version authority, untrusted registry input, the first agent instruction on clone, and host-shared npm state.

- Authority. package.json CLI pin, resolved core/content/types, and `directive --version` can disagree. The teaching-baseline gate couples only the README marker and the CLI pin.
- Untrusted input. Caret ranges let the public registry choose the engine. The existing control is exact `overrides` plus helper asserts.
- Shared state. `npm i -g` writes the host-global prefix. Module 2 and Lab 2 already classify that mutation as outside the disposable boundary.
- Agent envelope. The cold-start block is the sanctioned #2273 ladder. Managed `AGENTS.md` still contains `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` on the session-ritual card. A course-local README pin does not override that managed recovery.

Deterministic control for the graph is the fixture `overrides` + `verifyInstalledGraph` pattern already in tree.

## Road not taken

Rejected: close the issue with proposed-fix bullets 1–2 (pinned CLI command plus a caret-range sentence) because labs already lock the graph. That closes hole A and leaves hole B on the authoring/cold-start path, which is the P1 engine-baseline claim. Flip if the operator recuts P1 to unversioned-latest-CLI only and parks the graph lock on a later issue.

Also rejected: exact core/content/types dependencies inside the published `@deftai/directive` tarball. That would make a versioned global install sufficient. This repository cannot ship that change. The local control is already the fixture overrides.

## 4. Live latest has moved past the issue body's 0.119.6 instance
class: footnote

`npm view` on this host: `@deftai/directive`, `-core`, `-content`, and `-types` latest are all 0.119.7. The issue body's 0.119.6 `npx` line is the same failure class one compatible release earlier. The pnpm sibling command on README.md:8 is unversioned as well.
